verses.english: On the Bank of the Sutanu

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā anuruddho sāvatthiyaṁ viharati sutanutīre.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Anuruddha was staying near Sāvatthī on the bank of the Sutanu.

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yenāyasmā anuruddho tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā anuruddhena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
verses.english: Then several mendicants went up to Venerable Anuruddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ anuruddhaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “katamesaṁ āyasmā anuruddho dhammānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā mahābhiññataṁ patto”ti?
verses.english: “What things has Venerable Anuruddha developed and cultivated to attain great direct knowledge?”

verses.pali: “Catunnaṁ khvāhaṁ, āvuso, satipaṭṭhānānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā mahābhiññataṁ patto.
verses.english: “Reverends, I attained great direct knowledge by developing and cultivating the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Idhāhaṁ, āvuso, kāye kāyānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: I meditate observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.
I meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ—
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: imesaṁ khvāhaṁ, āvuso, catunnaṁ satipaṭṭhānānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā mahābhiññataṁ patto.
verses.english: I attained great direct knowledge by developing and cultivating these four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Imesañca panāhaṁ, āvuso, catunnaṁ satipaṭṭhānānaṁ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā hīnaṁ dhammaṁ hīnato abbhaññāsiṁ, majjhimaṁ dhammaṁ majjhimato abbhaññāsiṁ, paṇītaṁ dhammaṁ paṇītato abbhaññāsin”ti.
verses.english: And it was by developing and cultivating these four kinds of mindfulness meditation that I directly knew the lower principle as lower, the middle principle as middle, and the higher principle as higher.”
